chunks: Thus We gave Joseph authority in the land so that he lived wherever he liked. We bestow Our favours on whomsoever We please, and do not allow the reward of those who are good to go waste.
ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about God's mercy and Joseph's authority in the land?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse underscores the concept of divine preparation (istidraj) where Joseph’s rise to power was not merely political but a mechanism for executing God’s will, illustrating that authority is a trust granted to the righteous. It reinforces the principle that divine mercy is selective yet purposeful, ensuring that the rewards of the *muhsinin* (doers of good) are never lost, a key tenet in understanding theodicy and the fate of the prophets.
